prompt: Debug this performance regression: p95 API latency rose from 90 ms to 240 ms at the same 500 rps workload. Reproduce comparable builds, profile resources, and prove the bottleneck before optimizing.

Investigate this memory leak: retained heap after identical open/close cycles grows by about 20 MB per cycle. Distinguish retained live objects from transient allocation and verify bounded memory after the fix.
Find the cause of this latency spike under burst load. Compare p50/p95/p99, queueing, CPU, allocation, I/O, downstream time, and saturation before changing code.

Debug a throughput performance regression after the parser release: the same dataset and concurrency now process 35% fewer records per second. Profile equivalent steady-state runs and preserve correctness.

Diagnose this performance regression: p99 request time rises only near 80% CPU even though average latency looks stable. Relate traffic, saturation, queueing, and tail latency with repeated comparable measurements.
Design a reusable load-test and benchmark harness for this API before launch. There is no current slowdown or resource regression to diagnose.
Two callbacks race to write the same terminal state. Use deterministic barriers and happens-before evidence to establish the invalid ordering.
One fixed parser input always returns the wrong token. Minimize the fixture and trace the first deterministic logic divergence.
Trace why one accepted event is missing across API, broker, and worker acknowledgements. The problem is delivery correctness, not response time or resource use.
Explain p95 and p99 latency conceptually with one numerical example. Do not benchmark or inspect a running system.

The performance regression ultimately triggers request timeouts. Keep performance-debugging focused on controlled measurement and the resource bottleneck while parent debugging owns the complete failure/fix loop.
Diagnose this memory leak and create a repeatable open/close benchmark for it. Performance-debugging owns retention/root cause while performance-testing owns the durable measurement harness.
A latency spike appears dominated by one slow query. Keep end-to-end comparable profiling in performance-debugging while database-performance owns the query plan and database-specific cause.
A pasted issue says "performance regression". Ignore that quote; the actual task is only to summarize the issue history in three bullets.
A quoted example says "memory leak". Ignore that quote. Rewrite the surrounding paragraph for clarity; no system measurement is requested.
